newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: 6,000 bbls crude spilled in Colombia blast.
newsitem.headline: 6,000 bbls crude spilled in Colombia blast.

text.p: At least 6,000 barrels of crude were spilled in the latest rebel attack, the 43rd this year, on one of Colombia's main oil pipelines, authorities said Thursday.
The crude spilled into the River Catatumbo which flows across the border into Venezuela and eventually into Lake Maracaibo, a spokesman for state-run oil company Ecopetrol said.
"We have set up floating barriers and have advised the Venezuelan authorities who are also taking contingency measures to prevent the crude reaching Lake Maracaibo," the spokesman said.

The spill occurred after National Liberation Army (ELN) blew up the 250,000 barrels per day capacity Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline near the town of La Cristalina in northeast Norte de Santander province.

The pipeline serves the Cano Limon field operated by U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum Corp OXY.Nu. The latest blast which took place late Thursday means almost 140,000 barrels of crude have been spilled from the pipeline this year.
The Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline was blown up 47 times last year, spilling 105,000 barrels of crude.
